about.title: Orinda Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Orinda's traffic count is modest compared to nearby freeway hubs, but the SR-24 corridor still sees a steady flow of injury collisions each year, including morning commute crashes around Wednesday rush hour. Whether you were rear-ended near an SR-24 on-ramp, sideswiped merging onto the eastbound or westbound lanes, or hit on a local road like Moraga Way, the aftermath can mean medical bills, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster before you've even seen a doctor twice. We handle Orinda car accident claims and can evaluate the crash, deal with insurers, and explain what California's fault and damages rules mean for your specific situation. There's no cost for a free consultation, and if we take your case, we work on contingency — meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.title: Two-Year Window, But Evidence Fades Fast
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident lawsuit, but if a government-owned road or vehicle was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Getting an attorney involved early helps make sure evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness accounts near SR-24 doesn't disappear first.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you're found partially responsible for the crash — your compensation is simply adjusted to reflect your share of fault. We can help push back if the other driver's insurer tries to inflate your percentage of blame.

items.title: No Cap on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, so a serious injury from an Orinda-area collision isn't boxed in by an arbitrary ceiling. Our team can help make sure those losses are properly documented and valued, not just the medical bills.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney, since adjusters often use those statements to minimize claims later. Anything you say can be taken out of context or used to argue you were more at fault. Our team can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on SR-24 near Orinda but I'm not sure whose jurisdiction the road falls under?
items.answer: SR-24 is a state highway, so claims involving road design or maintenance issues could involve Caltrans, which carries a much shorter claim-filing deadline than the standard two years. This is one reason it helps to have an attorney looking at the facts of your Orinda crash sooner rather than later. We review these jurisdictional details as part of evaluating your case.

items.question: Is there really no cost for a free consultation after a car accident in Orinda?
items.answer: Correct — we don't charge anything for a free consultation to discuss your car accident. If we agree to take your case, we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid a fee if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost and no obligation to move forward after speaking with our team.
